speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Prime Minister given that special arrangements were made during the 2020 General Election for those on Stay-Home Notice at designated facilities to vote at these facilities away from other voters (a) whether the Government has any plans to provide similar arrangements for other groups of voters at future elections; and (b) whether the Government will also consider mail-in voting for Singaporeans who are overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The 2020 General Election, or GE2020, which was held amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighted two key issues in the electoral landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Second, from time to time, travel difficulties, such as in this pandemic, would make it difficult for Singaporeans working, studying or living overseas, to vote.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We recognise that many overseas Singaporeans remain engaged with Singapore and are keen to exercise their vote.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As the Member noted, the Elections Department, or ELD, made a special arrangement at GE2020 to allow voters serving Stay-Home Notice at designated hotels to cast their votes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For overseas Singaporeans, ELD had established overseas polling stations for them to cast their vote.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is because voting by paper ballot at polling stations remains the most transparent and secure method of voting that best ensures the integrity of the voting process and secrecy of votes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, ELD recognises that it may not be possible for various reasons, for some overseas Singaporeans to travel to these overseas polling stations to vote.
